A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OSF and SleepBench study. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical notation, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on sleep staging, event detection, disease prediction, heart-rate regression, scaling, and missing-channel robustness, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds measured baseline comparisons, corruption tests, subgroup evaluations, ablations, and computation-scaling results.

M1.justification: OSF retains the DINO-based Transformer, 50% channel masking, and temporal masking with ratios between 0.3 and 0.6. The SimCLR variant and patient-level aggregation methods already appear in v1. New normalization and masking-ratio ablations do not replace the proposed recipe.

E1.justification: The nine datasets remain unchanged. v2 extends disease prediction to SHHS, evaluates age subgroups in CFS and gender subgroups in MESA, including hypopnea detection, and adds inference scenarios involving noise and temporal channel detachment. These broaden coverage within the existing sleep domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against TS2Vec, ST-MEM, LSM-2, PedSleepMAE, and SleepGPT on sleep staging and hypopnea detection (Tables 4 and 26). PedSleepMAE was previously cited but not evaluated. Existing comparators remain; the few-shot tables' MTAE-to-MAE correction does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include separately fitted subgroup classifiers, corruption tests, normalization and masking-ratio controls, training-step sweeps, and accuracy, weighted F1, and Cohen's kappa evaluation. Existing splits and principal training settings remain. Scaling-table captions change ViT-80M to ViT-85M, matching v1's setup text; this correction does not establish reruns. Table 2's macro-averaging specification is newly disclosed, rather than an established metric change.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing analyses, v2 tests noise and temporal detachment, channel-masking ratios of 0.1/0.5/0.9, and min-max versus per-night z-score normalization. It also adds demographic comparisons, arousal/hypopnea embedding visualizations, and scaling with training steps (Tables 8, 30, 34, 39; Figures 11 and 13), substantially expanding robustness and design analysis.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without documented confidence intervals. v2 Table 28 introduces intervals for seven methods across four principal tasks and asserts statistical significance. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, but the confidence level, estimation procedure, and repeated-run or seed counts are unspecified; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and analyses while retaining most existing scores. Table 8 reports OSF hypopnea AUC below SleepFM under noise (69.4 versus 73.1), but above it under temporal detachment (76.2 versus 69.1). It also corrects SleepFM's full-data, multi-source SHHS AUPRC values for arousal, hypopnea, and desaturation from 89.5/76.3/75.9 to 86.3/77.0/75.0 (v1 Table 28; v2 Table 37).

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of masking and embedding aggregation remain unchanged. Neither version supplies formal scaling-law derivations or proofs, and v2's added scaling and disparity analyses do not introduce mathematical definitions or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three central findings and OSF contribution. However, v2 Section 2 explicitly reframes SleepBench as methodological infrastructure rather than a standalone contribution, modestly narrowing its contribution positioning. The additional experiments otherwise support retained headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting temporal-detachment robustness to masking, moderate masking to an information-versus-difficulty tradeoff, and normalization to cross-cohort variation. It discusses demographic fairness, less distinct rare-event embeddings, and capacity-dependent benefits from additional computation. Appendix E also qualifies the retained fewer-channel pre-training advantage from all tasks to most tasks.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that PedSleepMAE is pretrained on SleepBench while SleepGPT uses a released checkpoint, identifies 2,000 SHHS test epochs for the new UMAP analysis, and clarifies macro-averaging. The abstract drops the checkpoint-availability statement, and Section 2 adds a future processing-pipeline release pledge. The repository address remains unchanged; actual resource availability cannot be established from these wording changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and comparative positioning for TS2Vec, ST-MEM, LSM-2, and SleepGPT, alongside new HEARTS and SleepLM citations. It consistently cites DINOv2 and acknowledges community dataset-harmonization efforts when repositioning SleepBench. The principal related-work argument and section organization remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 inserts experimental discussion, adds Appendix D.4, Appendix F, and acknowledgments, and makes localized terminology and caption corrections, including MTAE to MAE. This is an extension with limited editing rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with tables for added baselines, corruption, uncertainty, demographic comparisons, metrics, disease prediction, and ablations, plus new event-label UMAP and training-step plots. Existing displays are redistributed while retaining their style. The reversed data-scaling/model-scaling panel titles are corrected in Figure 9 and in v1 Figure 12, now v2 Figure 14.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparisons and controlled masking and normalization ablations strengthen support for the practical pre-training recipe, while numerical and figure-label corrections improve consistency. These gains are limited by incomplete reporting of the new confidence intervals and overbroad interpretations: Table 27 includes worse hypertension AUPRC, and Table 30 includes greater MESA sleep-staging disparity, despite favorable general claims. The revision provides better supporting evidence without fully resolving its reliability and interpretation gaps.
